## Problem

The project management integration test modifies `customInstructions` on the real project and restores the original value only at the end of the test.

If `updateProject()`, `getProject()`, or an assertion fails before the restoration step, Jest exits the test early and the original project configuration may not be restored.

This can leave test-generated configuration in the project and affect subsequent tests or users.

## Suggestion

Move the restoration logic to a guaranteed cleanup path such as `afterAll`, or use a `try/finally`

`AsyncMemory.reset()` hardcodes `delete_col()` unconditionally, bypassing the `VectorStoreFactory.reset()` optimisation that `Memory.reset()` already uses. Sync `Memory.reset()` checks `hasattr(self.vector_store, "reset")` and calls `VectorStoreFactory.reset()` when available — which resets the store in-place without tearing it down and recreating it. The async counterpart skips this check entirely, so async users always get the slower `delete_col()` + full recreation path regardless of what the vector store supports.
